# Separate Colour

Splits a colour into RGB or HSV values so you can edit or compare each part.

`lfs.separate_colour` · Utilities

## How to use

Choose HSV to isolate hue, saturation or brightness.\
In HSV mode the R, G and B outputs carry those values in that order.

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Colour | `Colour` | lfs.colour | [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Colour to split, usually 0–1 per RGB channel. The default is black, with all channels at 0. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R | `R` | lfs.float | — | — | Red channel in RGB mode or hue in HSV mode. Hue runs from 0 to 1 around the colour wheel. |
| G | `G` | lfs.float | — | — | Green channel in RGB mode or saturation in HSV mode. HSV 0 is grey and 1 is fully saturated. |
| B | `B` | lfs.float | — | — | Blue channel in RGB mode or brightness in HSV mode. HSV 0 is black and 1 is full brightness. |

## Settings

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mode | `mode` | enum | rgb | rgb; hsv | Colour interpretation. RGB, the default, uses red, green and blue; HSV uses hue, saturation and brightness. |
